channel.title: Ranjita Naik — writing
channel.description: Notes on things I'm figuring out, explained from first principles.

item.title: Same steps, every time (Workflows)
item.description: The same job, run twice, done two different ways — and one check quietly never happened. A workflow is what you have when the steps are settled first.

item.title: A second conversation (Sub-agents)
item.description: It compared three analytics tools and wrote a good email. Then you asked how long to boil an egg, and twenty minutes of pricing pages were still sitting in the conversation.

item.title: Write it down once (Skills)
item.description: Your agent can reach your calendar and still book 4:30 on a Friday. Teaching it how you work turns out to be a folder and a file — and it barely costs anything.

item.title: Let your tools travel (MCP)
item.description: You got your agent to use one tool. Doing it again for every assistant and every service is the wall MCP removes. The surprising part is what it leaves alone.

item.title: Give your agent hands (Tools)
item.description: An AI can think brilliantly and still not do a thing. Tools are the piece that lets it act — and the surprising part is the model never sees the code, only your plain-English description.

item.title: Make it remember — give your AI agent a memory
item.description: Your agent starts every session with a blank memory, so you keep re-explaining yourself. A small file called CLAUDE.md fixes it — here's how, from first principles.

item.title: Build a webpage with an AI agent — no code
item.description: In about 20 minutes, get a real webpage open in your browser without writing a line of code — by describing what you want to an AI agent.

item.title: The Agent Loop (Think → Act → Observe) — an interactive explainer
item.description: Step through a real agent run: thoughts, tool calls, a failure and its recovery, with live token and cost counters.

item.title: What actually is an AI agent? A plain-English guide
item.description: The chatbot-vs-agent distinction, the three ingredients, and the questions worth asking before you build or buy one.

item.title: Start here: AI, LLMs and agents — explained from scratch
item.description: Assumes nothing — not even what LLM means. What an LLM is, what an agent is, and why people are talking about them.
